title: Efficient Performance-Aware GPU Sharing with Compatibility and Isolation through Kernel Space Interception
problem: GPUs are expensive resources that are often underutilized when used by single applications. Multiple workloads need to share GPU resources while maintaining performance isolation and compatibility, but existing GPU sharing solutions require significant modifications or introduce high virtualization overhead.
motivation: Efficient GPU sharing enables multi-tenant deployments and better resource utilization in data centers while maintaining performance predictability and reducing hardware costs.
method: When multiple applications request GPU resources, the system intercepts these requests at the kernel level—the lowest software layer where the OS directly controls hardware. Based on each workload's priority, it schedules GPU compute and memory access across the applications while enforcing isolation boundaries so one app's GPU use doesn't affect another. This kernel-level approach means existing applications don't need to be modified and you don't need to create virtual GPUs.
key_novelty: Intercepting GPU requests at the kernel level enables transparent, priority-aware GPU sharing and isolation without modifying applications or requiring virtual GPUs.
contributions: Kernel-space interception framework for intercepting and managing GPU operations transparently
Performance-aware scheduling algorithm balancing throughput and isolation across concurrent GPU workloads
Compatibility preservation enabling unmodified applications to share GPU resources
Efficient isolation mechanisms preventing performance interference between co-running applications

metrics.speedup: throughput improvement with multi-application GPU sharing

limitations: Kernel modifications required per GPU architecture; specific performance overhead analysis not evident from title alone.
primary_theme: GPU Resource Sharing via Kernel Interception
